title: Felix and the Letters
premise: Kestrel Dunmore, who inherited a failing vineyard and a mountain of debt instead of the thriving estate promised, agrees to a fake date with Felix Amara—a charming stranger met by chance—to survive the Dunmore family reunion. What begins as a performance turns painfully real, but Felix is hiding a secret: they are the estranged heir of the bank foreclosing on the vineyard, who walked away from that life and has been living under a changed identity. When the truth surfaces at the reunion's climax, Kestrel must decide whether love built on a lie can survive, and Felix must choose between the safety of invisibility and staying past the last train. They end by choosing each other openly, signing the vineyard's salvation together as an act of shared survival rather than debt.
about_author: Wendell Nakamura is a former sommelier turned novelist who writes love stories set in places that smell like rain on old stone. They live above a shuttered train station and insist all their characters deserve one more departure time.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Tasting Room
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Facing a family reunion where her aunt plans to announce the vineyard's foreclosure, Kestrel impulsively asks Felix—a warm, evasive stranger at her nearly empty tasting bar—to be her date. Felix agrees too quickly, as if fleeing something. Emotional beat: desperate hope disguised as a practical arrangement.

chapters.title: Rehearsing a Life
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Kestrel and Felix. Over a week of 'practice dates,' the fake couple builds real intimacy—shared stories, half-truths, a near-kiss interrupted by a foreclosure notice. Felix deflects every question about their past. Emotional beat: the terrifying discovery that pretending has stopped feeling like pretending.

chapters.title: Dessert and Confessions
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the reunion, Kestrel's cousin recognizes Felix as the vanished heir of Dunmore's bank, and the room turns. Felix confesses: they abandoned the family fortune and their old name, but their signature still seals the vineyard's fate. Kestrel walks into the storm. Emotional beat: betrayal, exposure, and the collapse of the safe fiction.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, closing with Felix's letter read aloud. At the empty station, Kestrel asks Felix to miss the last train and stay—not as a stranger or an heir, but as themselves. Felix chooses to fight the foreclosure from the inside, and they return to the vineyard together. Emotional beat: choosing visibility, memory, and each other over survival by disappearance.
